correctness.rationale: The frozen claims are mathematically consistent; the repair is not a correction of a false root coefficient. For the final statement the last-reset identity uses a compactly supported directly Riemann integrable one-flight kernel with its hitting endpoint excluded. The nonarithmetic renewal theorem integrates it to the uniform spatial expectation, and each finite-time support is finite. The rational comparison follows from the only unit-circle pole at 1 of the coprime duration generating function and the finite list of allowed ages. For the added quantitative assertion, the locally finite set of renewal times gives a left limit of the mean, and only paths that reset at t=ja+kb contribute a jump of normalized size one. Irrationality makes the representation by j,k unique, so the jump is the probability of the disjoint permutations of those duration draws, binom(j+k,j)p^j q^k. At j=floor(np), k=n−j the time is nμ+O(1) and Stirling gives a jump asymptotic to (2πnpq)^(−1/2). At least one of the right value and left limit differs from 1/2 by half the jump; the latter can be approximated within 1/n at a time less than 1/n earlier. This proves the repaired limsup bound with constant √μ/(2√(2πpq)). Independently, the normalized mean transform is B/D with B=1/z−[p(1−e^(−az))/a+q(1−e^(−bz))/b]/z². At the known quadratic root sequence D′→μ>0, both exponentials tend to one and B=1/z+O(1/|z|²), so no cancellation occurs. A transform analytic across the axis in a fixed strip would violate D(z)(G(z)+1/(2z))=B(z) at these zeros. Frozen code was inspected, not run: its rational phase samples and numerical checks at several approximants to √2 are finite diagnostics, not certification of the new bound or the pole sequence.
residual_risks: The limsup inequality is not a matching upper rate. Only fresh starts with two positive durations and immediate right-continuous resets are covered. Noncancellation is claimed along the specified near-axis sequence, not for all zeros.

value.rationale: A known near-axis spectral expansion alone is not credited as added value. The freshly reset process distinguishes stationary occupation from transient relaxation of an elementary physical observable. The exact jump law and uniform-in-arithmetic-type-of-irrational lower exponent show that deviations of order at least t⁻¹/² survive along some times for every irrational ratio, without needing fine Diophantine constants. That is stronger information than merely excluding exponentials, while the pole proof separately identifies the spectral obstruction in the actual observable rather than in an arbitrary test. The two-atom model is the simplest genuinely random atomic version of the initiating model, not an arbitrary parameter sample.
residual_risks: No claim of the optimal upper rate, or that the behavior persists after smoothing, averaging in time, or introducing continuous speed noise.
